jobs.title: Recruitment Manager
jobs.description: Wil jij op operationeel niveau bouwen aan de mensen die het onderwijs van duizenden leerlingen versterken? Als Resource Manager bij Lyceo in Leiden krijg je een sleutelpositie binnen een landelijke marktleider die volop groeit. Een baan met directe impact, veel verantwoordelijkheid en volop ruimte om recruitment en capaciteitsmanagement verder te professionaliseren. Taken Maak het verschil als Recruitment Manager Als Resource Manager zorg je ervoor dat Lyceo nu en in de toekomst beschikt over de juiste begeleiders om scholen en leerlingen tijdig te ondersteunen. Je bent eindverantwoordelijk voor hun beschikbaarheid, kwaliteit en inzetbaarheid. Je maakt deel uit van het MT en rapporteert rechtstreeks aan de directie van Lyceo. Met ondersteuning van het datateam bepaal je welke begeleiders waar en wanneer nodig zijn. Op basis daarvan laat je gerichte recruitmentacties uitvoeren en geef je richting aan selectie, matching en onboarding. Met KPI’s bewaak je de instroom, retentie, vervulling en doorlooptijden en stuur je gericht bij. Daarnaast optimaliseer je processen en geef je leiding aan een team met onder andere een Recruiter en een Coördinator Matching en Onboarding. Samen met de Operationeel Manager zorg je voor voldoende geschikte mensen en een succesvolle uitvoering van alle onderwijsprojecten. Bij afwezigheid kunnen jullie elkaars verantwoordelijkheden overnemen. Kortom, jij pakt de regie bij het: • realiseren van voldoende gerichte instroom en een kwalitatief sterke recruitment, selectie en onboarding; • verbinden van vraag en aanbod op basis van regio, vakgebied, onderwijstype, beschikbaarheid en reisbereidheid; • voorspellen, bewaken en bijsturen van de capaciteitsbehoefte met data en KPI’s; • optimaliseren van recruitment en instroomprocessen en adviseren over selectiecriteria, retentie en capaciteit; • aansturen van het team en bewaken van het recruitmentbudget. Vereisten Voor deze vacature neem jij mee: Je vertaalt recruitmentdoelstellingen naar concrete acties en stuurt met data op kwaliteit, instroom en capaciteit. Historische resultaten combineer je met verwachtingen en ontwikkelingen in de markt. Ook wanneer nog niet alles vaststaat, kijk je vooruit, maak je keuzes en stuur je tijdig bij. Als leidinggevende sta je dicht bij je team, geef je richting en neem je mensen met positieve energie mee. Ervaring binnen recruitment, arbeidsbemiddeling, detachering of vergelijkbare dienstverlening helpt je om wisselende capaciteitsvragen snel te doorgronden. Vink jij deze checklist ook af? • minimaal hbo werk- en denkniveau; • ervaring met recruitment, werving en selectie; • leidinggevende ervaring binnen recruitment, capaciteitsmanagement of een vergelijkbare dienstverlenende omgeving; • ervaring met het sturen op data en KPI’s binnen recruitment of capaciteitsplanning; • ervaring met het optimaliseren van recruitment- of instroomprocessen. Jouw werkgebied Jouw nieuwe werkplek bevindt zich in Leiden, vlak bij Leiden Centraal. Vanuit het kantoor werk je nauw samen met de verschillende afdelingen van Lyceo. Dankzij de ligging nabij het centraal station is de werkplek goed bereikbaar met het openbaar vervoer. Benefits Als Recruitment Manager kun jij rekenen op: Een verantwoordelijke functie bij een groeiende onderwijsorganisatie waar ontwikkeling niet alleen voor leerlingen centraal staat. Lyceo biedt je ruimte voor initiatief, eigenaarschap en nieuwe ideeën. Via de Lyceo Academie blijf je bovendien zelf leren en krijg je volop mogelijkheden om binnen de organisatie door te groeien. Op basis van een fulltime dienstverband krijg je daarbovenop: • een verantwoordelijke functie van 32 tot 40 uur per week, waarbij je tijdens de drukke periodes in het schooljaar flexibel beschikbaar bent; • 25 vakantiedagen, waarvan je naar rato 10 vakantiedagen opneemt in de zomervakantie; • de mogelijkheid om 5 extra verlofdagen bij te kopen; • 8% vakantiegeld, uitbetaald in mei; • reiskostenvergoeding per kilometer of volledige vergoeding van OV

jobs.title: Staff Engineer - Fintech
jobs.description: <div class="content-intro"><h4><strong>Help make the world more hospitable </strong></h4> <p>The hospitality industry is uniquely human, and it deserves technology that’s just as inspiring as the people behind it. At Mews, we’re transforming the industry with a platform that helps hotels run smarter, move faster and create better guest experiences.</p> <p>You’ll work with smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do. You’ll have autonomy and the trust to make good decisions and move quickly. And you’ll enjoy a real sense of purpose as you see the impact of what we’re building.</p> <p>If you’re motivated by ownership, curiosity and meaningful impact, and are driven to deliver consistent high performance, you’ll feel at home here.</p> <h4><strong>About the role</strong></h4> <p>Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:</p></div><p>You will own the agents, skills and standards that let a tribe of product builders move quickly on payments without the architecture fragmenting. Hotels take payments across regions and through providers that each behave differently, and Payment Interfaces exists to give customers one coherent payment experience on top of several PSPs. Embedded payments at this depth is rare among European SaaS companies, so the problems here are ones few engineers get to work on.</p> <p>You will be a Staff Engineer in the Payment Interfaces team, part of the Fintech tribe. You will report to the Director of Product and Engineering, sit in the tribe’s leadership group, and work alongside product builders, other staff engineers and product managers. No one reports to you, so your influence comes from the architecture, tools and standards that other people choose to work in.</p> <p>The team integrates several PSPs depending on region and conditions. When integrations drift apart, builders slow down and quality suffers. This role exists to keep them coherent by encoding what good looks like into tools and agents, so every builder meets the standard by default.</p> <h4><strong>What you would do</strong>&nbsp;</h4> <ul> <li>Own the tribe’s engineering agents, skills and context, and encode architectural standards, review logic and quality gates into them so the standard is met by default.</li> <li>Build an AI first responder for customer tickets about payment issues, with clear rules for when it answers and when it hands over to a person.</li> <li>Stay hands-on for the hardest technical problems: migrations, system-wide refactors and long-lived architecture decisions across PSP integrations.</li> <li>Keep Payment Interfaces integrations coherent as PSPs and regional requirements change, collaborating with builders who own their own work.</li> <li>Coach builders and fix off-standard outcomes at the cause, so the lesson sticks.</li> </ul> <p><strong>AI Fluency Level 4:</strong> in this role, that means you build the AI systems the tribe works in, not only use them. You design the agents, skills and evaluations that builders rely on every day, make the engineering decisions about how they behave, and set the rules for when an AI answer can stand and when a person must step in.</p> <p><em>For more information on AI fluency at Mews, please refer to “<a href="https://mews.atlassian.net/wiki/external/YWI5ZGUyMGQ3MjU2NGRmNjlkZGEyYTg2NTVmZGE0OTU">AI Fluency at Mews: A Comprehensive Guide for Candidates</a>” on Confluence.</em></p> <h4><strong>What you would bring</strong>&

jobs.title: hbo-stage Bedrijfskunde: Digitalisering en Procesoptimalisatie van communicatie
jobs.description: hbo- afstudeerstage, vanaf februari 2027 Ben jij die enthousiaste hbo-student die het leuk vindt om organisatievraagstukken te onderzoeken en processen te verbeteren? Dit is jouw uitdaging Het Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS) wil het gebruik van papieren post verminderen en de mogelijkheden voor digitale communicatie verder uitbreiden. Dit geldt zowel voor de communicatie met bedrijven als met personen. Tijdens deze stage richt je je specifiek op de communicatie met individuele onderzoekspersonen. Op dit moment benadert het CBS onderzoekspersonen in eerste instantie vrijwel altijd via een brief op het huisadres. Digitale communicatie, bijvoorbeeld via e-mail, biedt kansen om dit proces efficiënter, flexibeler en toekomstbestendiger in te richten. Er lopen binnen het CBS al verschillende initiatieven om meer gebruik te maken van e-mailadressen, maar er zijn ook nog belangrijke vraagstukken die onderzocht moeten worden. Denk bijvoorbeeld aan de volgende vragen: Hoe kan het CBS op een effectieve manier e-mailadressen van onderzoekspersonen verzamelen en beheren? Welke juridische en privacyvoorwaarden gelden voor het opbouwen en gebruiken van een e-maildatabase? Welke technische aanpassingen en voorzieningen zijn nodig om digitale communicatie mogelijk te maken? Hoe moeten de bestaande werkprocessen worden aangepast om digitale communicatie goed te ondersteunen? Hoe kunnen we ervoor zorgen dat onderzoekspersonen op een toegankelijke en betrouwbare manier digitaal benaderd worden? Samen met het Waarneeminnovatie Team en collega's van de afdeling Dataverzameling ga je dit vraagstuk onderzoeken. Je brengt de huidige situatie in kaart, onderzoekt mogelijkheden voor verbetering en werkt toe naar concrete aanbevelingen voor het CBS. Dit is jouw stageplek bij CBS Heerlen Je gaat aan de slag in het Team Waarneeminnovatie. Dit team valt binnen de afdeling Dataverzameling. We zijn een jong, divers en vooral enthousiast team dat als doel heeft de waarneming van het CBS te vernieuwen en te verbeteren.  Dit breng jij mee Je volgt een hbo-opleiding Bedrijfskunde of een soortgelijke opleiding. Je hebt interesse in procesoptimalisatie, digitalisering en organisatieverandering. Je bent nieuwsgierig, onderzoekend en neemt graag initiatief. Je vindt het leuk om met verschillende betrokkenen binnen een organisatie in gesprek te gaan. Je hebt een proactieve, positieve en assertieve houding en denkt in oplossingen, staat open voor feedback en gaat uitdagingen met enthousiasme aan. Omdat tijdens de stage alle communicatie – zowel mondeling als schriftelijk – in het Nederlands plaatsvindt, is een goede beheersing van de Nederlandse taal noodzakelijk. Dit kun je van ons verwachten Een fijne leeromgeving waarin je: samen met ervaren vakmensen bestaande processen analyseert en verbeterkansen herkent; zelfstandig een praktijkgericht onderzoek of experiment opzet; aan de slag gaat met het in kaart brengen van verschillende organisatorische, juridische en technische belangen en randvoorwaarden rondom digitale communicatie; leert om onderzoeksresultaten te vertalen naar concrete, onderbouwde en uitvoerbare aanbevelingen voor het CBS. Voor jouw inzet ontvang je een stagevergoeding van € 800,- bruto per maand (op basis van 40 uur per week). Samen met je stagebegeleider stem je af hoe je hybride kunt werken, met flexibele werktijden en de optie om deels vanuit huis aan jouw stageopdracht te werken. Dit zijn onze voorwaarden Het betreft een stageopdracht en geen werkervaringsplek. Voordat je aan de stage begint verwachten we dat je vanuit de onderwijsinstelling een stagebegeleider hebt, waarmee de stage is afgestemd en concrete leerdoelen zijn afgesproken. Deze stageopdracht is bedoeld voor studenten die momenteel staan ingeschreven bij een onderwijsinstelling; afgestudeerden komen niet in aanmerking. Find Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

HOW YOU'LL MOVE US FORWARD Lawyers and tax advisors ask a question in GenIA-L and get a reliable answer. That answer is what they see. What you build is everything needed to make it happen: the backend. These are the systems and connections that keep our AI product fast, secure and reliable. You join the AI team and work with our AI engineers every day. They make the product smart; you make sure that intelligence actually reaches the user. After six months, you know the code well and have shipped several new features. After that, you choose the direction you want to grow in: more towards AI, for example by improving the quality of our AI answers, or more towards DevOps, for example by improving how we automatically test and release software. You build APIs and services: the connections that let the different parts of the platform talk to each other. You keep an eye on code quality and make sure we follow good practices and standards. At least 3 years of experience building Python applications that run in production and are actually used by customers. Experience with FastAPI and Pydantic. Experience with LangChain or LangGraph is a plus. You have built production-grade APIs that work reliably for real users. You work independently within a team and don’t need hand-holding. Knowledge of Postgres, GraphQL or MongoDB is a plus. Some DevOps knowledge is nice to have, for example working with GitHub Actions and Helm. WHAT YOU'RE SIGNING UP FOR You join the AI team with one other backend engineer, three AI engineers and a Product Owner. jobs.description: De afdeling Lenen, Sparen en Retailbeleggen (LSR) houdt toezicht op financiële producten en diensten voor consumenten, zoals hypotheken, kredieten, sparen, betalen en beleggen. We zorgen dat informatie duidelijk is en dat online dienstverlening goed toegankelijk is. Samen zorgen we dat het klantbelang centraal staat, vooral voor kwetsbare groepen.   Ons toezicht richt zich op het herkennen en aanpakken van risico’s voor consumenten. We willen dit zo snel en effectief mogelijk doen. Om meer impact te maken, gebruiken we data op een slimme manier. Daarbij zoeken we continu naar signalen, toetsen we aannames en brengen we risico’s en mogelijke blinde vlekken in beeld. Zo kunnen we sneller inspelen op veranderingen in de financiële sector.   De vraagstukken waar je aan werkt zijn vaak nieuw, complex en actueel. Denk aan risico’s rond Buy Now Pay Later, online beleggingsplatformen, AI-toepassingen of ontwikkelingen in de cryptomarkt. Jouw analyses dragen direct bij aan keuzes die de AFM maakt in haar toezicht.   Dit ga je doen: Samenwerken met toezichthouders om risico’s voor consumenten tijdig te signaleren. Ontwikkelen van dataproducten die inzichten vertalen naar gerichte acties. Implementeren van betrouwbare en schaalbare oplossingen voor effectiever toezicht. Visualiseren van resultaten in dashboards die toezichthouders ondersteunen. Kansen signaleren om processen slimmer in te richten en repetitief werk te automatiseren. Ook kijkt het team naar risico’s van nieuwe technologie in de financiële sector. Zo spelen we een belangrijke rol in het tijdig herkennen van risico’s.   De deadline voor deze vacature is 25 november 2026. Voor deze complexe systeemimplementaties en integratieprojecten zoeken we een zeer ervaren projectmanager. Je leert de verzekeringsbranche kennen en klanten helpen. Dat doe je niet alleen: je werkt samen met enthousiaste collega’s in een projectteam. Voordelen voor de sollicitant Als projectmanager krijg je veel verantwoordelijkheid, help je klanten en samen met je projectteam zet je mooie resultaten neer. Je kunt deels thuiswerken, deels op ons kantoor in Woerden en bij verschillende klanten in Nederland. Tijdelijk werken vanuit het buitenland kan ook dankzij onze workation-regeling (maximaal 30 dagen aaneengesloten per jaar). Bij ons draait het om klantgericht werken én werkplezier. Daarom is er volop ruimte voor ontspanning en plezier. Denk aan een levend tafelvoetbaltoernooi, pubquiz en een bier- & wijnproeverij. Ons actieve Fun-team zorgt elke maand weer voor iets leuks. En als je reislust nog niet is gestild met 25 vakantiedagen en een workation, dan kun je zelfs tot 20 extra verlofdagen bijkopen. Genoeg redenen om verder te lezen en te ontdekken of deze functie iets voor jou is, toch? Een voorbeeld van je werkdag Opstarten: Aan het begin van je werkdag heb je een dagstart met zowel collega’s als projectteamleden van de klant. Hierin bespreken jullie de voortgang, resultaten en eventuele hulpvragen. Na de dagstart: Allereerst neem je nog wat tijd met een van de consultants naar aanleiding van de dagstart. Je coacht en begeleidt de consultant en helpt deze met een hulpvraag. Vervolgens ga je aan de slag met het opstellen van de voortgangsrapportage. Hiermee zorg je voor proactieve en transparante rapportage over het project aan de klant. De stuurgroep met de klant is volgende week, vandaag spreek je samen met de delivery manager deze stuurgroep voor. Wat zijn de belangrijkste punten voor de klant en voor CCS en hoe vliegen we die aan. Na de lunch: Je checkt nog een paar tickets qua voortgang op het planboard, waarbij je de samenhang met de planning checkt. Vervolgens ga je naar de werksessie met het CCS projectmanagement guild. Hier werken jullie aan tickets om de CCS Prince2Agile projectmethodiek verder te verbeteren. Hierna heb je nog een afspraak met je collega van sales voor afstemming over een mogelijk vervolgproject bij de klant. Wie jij bent De ideale kandidaat beschikt over daadkracht, doorzettingsvermogen, enthousiasme en drive om projecten succesvol te leiden en verbeteringen door te voeren om te komen tot nog efficiëntere en klantgerichte projecten. Jij herkent jezelf in de volgende punten: · Je wordt blij van projectmanagement en blijft kalm bij verschuivende prioriteiten; · Je hebt bewezen ervaring met het succesvol uitvoeren van productsoftware-implementaties in een complexe, maar klantgerichte omgeving, binnen budget, planning en scope; · Je hebt ruime ervaring met diverse projectmanagement en delivery methodieken, bij voorkeur een Prince2-, Ipma of PMI of Agile / scrum certificaat; · Je vindt, net als wij, klanttevredenheid het uitgangspunt. Daarbij ben je in staat om de klantverwachtingen helder te analyseren, te managen en actief bij te sturen waar nodig; · Je beheerst de Nederlandse en Engelse taal uitstekend in woord en geschrift; · Jouw persoonlijkheid kenmerkt zich door: gestructureerd, motiverend, communicatief sterk, duidelijk, open, tikje eigenwijs, enthousiast, relativerend, creatief en pragmatisch; · Je haalt energie uit het opstellen en bewaken van planningen, analyseren van gegevens en opstellen van duidelijke, gestructureerde rapportages en presentaties; · Je hebt minimaal een afgeronde bachelor, bij voorkeur richting bedrijfskunde, bedrijfseconomie en/of informatica. jobs.title: Security Engineer
jobs.description: At bunq, we’re on a mission to Make Life Easy for our users by creating the most user-centric banking experience out there. That starts with keeping their data safe. As AI makes attackers faster, we’re seeing more critical zero-day vulnerabilities than ever, and we need to stay ahead of them. That’s where you come in. As our  Security Engineer , you’ll own how 700 colleagues get secure access to our systems, and you’ll help defend bunq against attacks as they happen. You’ll design and build security processes that AI can’t run on its own, and automate everything that it can. Take Ownership 🚀 You’ll keep bunq secure, from access control to incident response. Here’s how you’ll do it: Own access control governance in Okta Identity Governance, automating how access is granted, revoked and reviewed, so every employee and contractor has the right access from day one. Investigate and triage security incidents and vulnerability findings, decide whether they’re malicious, and escalate or fix them fast. Drive the replacement of our security monitoring system with an AI-based platform that detects and stops threats automatically, and build automations so the team can focus on real security issues. You’ve worked hands-on as a security engineer, investigating and triaging security incidents. You write code to automate security work, not just to run scripts. You’ve worked with identity governance and know how to build secure login and access solutions. You communicate clearly with stakeholders, especially under pressure when someone is locked out or an incident hits. You bring engineering experience. Consultancy experience alone isn’t the right fit. Curious to see how we make life easy? - try the bunq app , it only takes 5 minutes to sign up. Your space to perform We give you the space and the tools you need to succeed 💪 🤟 Great, international colleagues who share your mindset 👩‍💻 Hybrid setup: after 3 months in-office, work 2 days remote, 3 days in-office weekly. 🧳 Digital Nomad Program: After your first year, enjoy up to 20 days per year to work while traveling, combining flexibility with strong team collaboration 🚀 We reward tenure with a dedicated travel budget: €1.5k after 2 years and €3k after 4 years to visit another core office. 📚 We support growth with bunq Academy and €1500 annual learning budget 🧘 €60 monthly allowance via Alleo by Epassi, rolling over monthly and resetting annually 🚌﻿ Travel expenses are covered whether you come walking or by bike, bus or car (though we prefer green choices 🌳) ﻿💻 A MacBook so you can Get Shit Done with us 🥦 Delicious lunches from our fabulous in-house chefs with vegan and vegetarian options 💰 An optional pension plan with monthly contribution from bunq 💸 Monthly contribution to your phone and internet bills 🍻 Friday drinks and other celebrations - bunq style﻿ All new hires are subject to Pre-employment Screening (PES), which includes checks conducted by our third-party partner, Zinc. jobs.title: Senior Cloud Engineer
jobs.description: At Luscii, we're creating space for care by developing and improving digital healthcare applications that make a real difference in people's lives through several applications. From Luscii Thuismeten, which helps healthcare professionals monitor patients remotely, to OMRON Connect, connecting millions of people with their health data through OMRON devices, and other applications that expand the possibilities of digital healthcare. Together with healthcare professionals and partners around the world, we're working towards a future where people receive the right care in the right place. As our Senior Cloud Engineer, you'll help shape and modernise the cloud infrastructure behind these applications, building a reliable, scalable and future-proof foundation for millions of users worldwide. Our applications have different histories, architectures and technical challenges. OMRON Connect, for example, runs on an AWS backend serving several million monthly active users. Parts of its infrastructure still carry legacy, including manual processes, scattered knowledge, inconsistent observability and release processes that make changes slower and riskier than they should be. We're working towards a more consistent engineering foundation across our applications. Think Infrastructure as Code, cloud-native and event-driven architecture where it adds value, safe continuous deployment and observability by default. We're bringing more senior engineering expertise in-house to turn that ambition into concrete technical decisions, shared standards and a roadmap our teams can own. And that's where you come in 😉 Your role You will work across our engineering teams, helping shape the cloud infrastructure behind our digital healthcare applications. Your focus will be on making the right architectural decisions, modernising existing platforms and enabling teams to independently build, maintain and improve their systems. This isn't a greenfield architecture exercise. You will be improving live healthcare platforms while balancing technical improvements with product delivery, security, regulatory requirements and the realities of working with stakeholders across different countries, including the Netherlands and Japan. What you will be doing, among others: Own and evolve the Cloud & Backend roadmap, translating the engineering vision into clear priorities, trade-offs and next steps. Drive cross-team architecture decisions to a close, making sure decisions are transparent, documented and followed through. Establish shared technical standards and guardrails that allow teams to work autonomously without creating unnecessary dependencies. Work hands-on with engineers on AWS and Terraform, reviewing designs and pull requests and challenging technical choices where needed. Coach and pair with engineers, helping knowledge spread across teams and supporting the growth of seniority and ownership. Work with product owners, QA, engineering leadership and colleagues in Japan to balance technical direction with product, regulatory, security and cost considerations. Help move the platform towards automated infrastructure, safer deployments and stronger observability without relying on a big-bang rewrite. The responsibilities outlined above reflect how we currently envision this role. As we continue to grow and evolve, the scope and focus of the position may naturally change, influenced by your own ideas and insights. The way we work is built around the belief that everyone's input matters. If you see opportunities to improve the way we do things, or believe a process could be designed differently to achieve a better outcome, we encourage you to bring those ideas forward. Discuss them with your teammates, challenge the status quo, and help shape how we move forward together. Why Luscii? Read more about working at Luscii / OMRON and how we work as a team. jobs.title: Data Platform Manager
jobs.description: About the role As Data Platform Manager you will own Destinus's company data platform. Built on Microsoft Fabric, it brings together data from our different systems, and it serves the reporting and data agents that production, supply chain, program management, and finance work from every week. You will own its architecture: how OneLake and our lakehouses are structured, how data lands in them from the systems we run, and how it holds up as more of the business comes to depend on it. You will lead a small team of data engineers — setting direction, reviewing their work, growing them — and you will keep building yourself. You are also the person who makes our AI ambitions possible: the foundation behind our data agents and our Company Brain is yours to design and deliver. At Destinus we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing, building advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) across three European plants. The data you will work with is physical — parts, build progress, shortages, non-conformances — and the questions asked of it get harder each year as we grow. If you want a platform you can still shape rather than one already set in concrete, this is a good moment to arrive. What You'll Do Own the architecture of our Microsoft Fabric estate end to end — OneLake, our lakehouses and their bronze, silver, and gold layers, workspace and domain structure, naming conventions, and the standards that keep it coherent as it grows. Lead, mentor, and grow a small team of data engineers: set priorities, review code, raise the technical bar, and develop the people. Stay hands-on. You will build pipelines, notebooks, and Delta tables yourself, not only direct others who do. Own the integrations that land data in OneLake from our source systems — ERP, HR, shopfloor, quality, and the business applications that come after them — choosing sensibly between Data Factory pipelines, dataflows, shortcuts, and mirroring for each source. Own the gold layer and the semantic models built on it, so that Power BI reads from one governed source rather than from copies scattered around the business. Work closely with our Business Operations & Data Specialists, who represent the business owners of each domain: turn their requirements into the right gold tables, agree definitions with them, and give them a platform they can query, validate, and explain to the business with confidence. Own lineage across the estate: know what feeds what, be able to prove it to an auditor, and make dependencies visible rather than tribal knowledge. Build the data foundation for our AI programme — the lakehouse structures, pipelines, and knowledge graph behind our Fabric data agents and our Company Brain — and deliver it to a standard that can be trusted with a real question. Design and maintain the OneLake security and access model together with your team: workspace roles, access groups, and the controls that decide who sees what in the lake. Keep the platform reliable, observable, and cost-aware: monitoring, alerting, recovery, and disciplined use of our Fabric capacity — including knowing what a runaway notebook costs us. Requirements What You’ll Need Requirements Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field. 5-8 years of data engineering experience, including real ownership of a lakehouse architecture rather than only delivering against someone else's. Hands-on Microsoft Fabric experience is strongly preferred — OneLake, lakehouses, Delta tables, the SQL analytics endpoint, Data Factory pipelines, Spark notebooks, and semantic models in Direct Lake mode. If your depth is in Azure Synapse, Databricks, or Data Lake Storage Gen2 and you have since moved onto Fabric in earnest, we will take that seriously. Strong command of the medallion pattern and of Delta Lake in practice: partitioning, schema evolution, table maintenance, and why a gold table behaves the way it does. Genuinely hands-on. Strong SQ

jobs.title: Business Operations & Data Specialist (Production & Quality)
jobs.description: About the role Behind every well-run plant is a shared understanding of how it is performing — and that understanding has to be built. As a Business Operations & Data Specialist focused on Production & Quality at Destinus, you are the bridge between the people who run our plants and the data that describes them. Plant managers, production leads, and quality engineers own the processes; our lakehouse holds the data those processes create. Your job is to connect the two, so that every production and quality figure, from the shopfloor to the leadership team, is defined by the business, built on the lakehouse, and trusted by both. This is as much an operations role as a reporting one. You will translate what the business needs to know into what the data platform has to deliver, working with our Data Engineers on the production and quality data in the lakehouse and turning it into the reporting used across three European plants, including our Digital Shopfloor Management Solution, relied on by more than 300 people. You will also go to where the data is created and make it better there — improving how it is captured, automating what is still manual, and helping three plants work to one standard. At Destinus, we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing — bringing speed, precision, and innovation to every process that powers our advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). Our operations span multiple plants and teams, and your work will directly support the reliability, efficiency, and excellence required for mission-critical production. Join us in shaping the next era of aerospace operations. What You'll do Be the go-to contact between the business owners of production and quality data — plant managers, production leads, and quality engineers — and our lakehouse: turn their questions into clear data requirements, and the data back into answers they can act on. Own the production and quality portfolio end to end: define the KPI, improve the process behind it, build the dashboard, and stand behind the number. Own the production and quality domain in our lakehouse: know which tables and fields hold what, where each comes from, and who owns it at source — and keep that knowledge documented rather than in your head. Partner with our Data Engineers on the curated (gold) layer for production and quality: specify the tables, fields, and business rules the business needs, and validate the result against what actually happens on the shopfloor before anyone relies on it. Set and monitor data quality checks for your domain, and route each issue to the right owner — the person entering the data, the system configuration, or the pipeline — until it is fixed. Maintain and continuously improve Power BI dashboards tracking production and quality performance across all three plants, built on certified lakehouse data rather than side spreadsheets. Describe production and quality data in plain business language — what each field means, who owns it, and how sensitive it is — for our shared meanings layer, so that colleagues and our AI assistants can use it correctly without having to ask you first. Automate what is manual today: recurring reports, data collection, and the preparation behind daily and weekly performance routines. Support the standardisation of ways of working across the three plants, partnering with our Lean Operations Specialist so that measurement and improvement pull in the same direction. Requirements What You’ll Need Bachelor's or Master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Quality Management, or a related field. Experience in a production or quality environment; aerospace or another regulated industry is highly preferred. Solid understanding of manufacturing and quality metrics — throughput, cycle time, OEE, scrap and rework, first-pass yield — and of quality processes such as non-conformance handling, customer complaints and field returns, root cause analysis, and corrective actions. Je hebt ervaring met A/B-tests, holdout-tests en hypothese gedreven werken. Je hebt commercieel gevoel: je denkt net zo graag mee over het aanbod als over de cijfers erachter. Je bent een sterke sparringpartner: je daagt collega’s uit met data en laat je zelf ook uitdagen. Je bent kritisch, hands-on en niet bang om de status quo uit te dagen. Our Systems Integration Team is seeking a Model-Based Systems Engineer to build the tools and framework we use to design the systems that operate our VIO and QPU technology. This role is focused on establishing QuantWare’s MBSE methodology and turning knowledge from cryogenics, wiring, control electronics and software into a single, executable system model. You will define how we model our systems and build the libraries, analyses and integrations that make the model useful day to day. Working closely with processor, hardware and software teams, you will play an important role in enabling the design of the large-scale quantum computers built around VIO-powered QPUs. What are you going to do? Define and own QuantWare’s MBSE methodology, modelling conventions and architecture framework for quantum computing systems, covering the quantum processor, cryostat, signal chain, control and readout electronics, and software stack. Select, set up and maintain the MBSE toolchain (e.g. SysML v2, Capella or Cameo), including version control, model reviews and integration with existing engineering tools. Build reusable model libraries for key subsystems, including QPU interfaces, cryogenic wiring and attenuation, microwave signal paths, and control electronics. Develop automated analyses on top of the model, such as heat-load, signal-integrity and noise budgets, channel counts, scalability, and full-system metrics such as power consumption as qubit counts grow. Establish requirements traceability from customer and system-level requirements down to component specifications and verification tests. Connect the system model to simulation and measurement data, creating a digital thread between design and test. Support system architecture and trade studies for new VIO and QPU generations and customer system integrations. Drive adoption across the company, training and supporting engineers in using the models and tools in their day-to-day work. Strong working knowledge of SysML (v1 and/or v2) and at least one MBSE tool, such as Cameo, Capella or equivalent. Proficiency in Python for model automation, analysis and tool integration via APIs. A solid track record in requirements engineering and verification of complex, multidisciplinary hardware systems. Strong organisational and communication skills. You thrive in a cross-disciplinary environment and are comfortable taking ownership from day one. Bonus Points Experience with cryogenic, RF/microwave or precision instrumentation systems, or direct experience with superconducting quantum hardware. Background in high-tech, semiconductor, aerospace or scientific instrumentation industries. Experience introducing MBSE into an organisation and driving its adoption. Familiarity with SysML v2 APIs, digital thread concepts or co-simulation (e.g. FMI), as well as systems engineering standards such as ISO/IEC 15288. Don't tick every box? Apply anyway! Du agierst auf einem makrotechnischen Level und sorgst mit deinem tiefen technischen Know-how dafür, dass Gebäudeinfrastruktur und fortschrittliche Automatisierungstechnik wie ein einziger, fehlerfreier Organismus zusammenarbeiten.&nbsp;Während ein separates Automation Team das reine Material Handling Equipment (MHE) betreut, steuerst du das große Ganze: Du managest hohe Budgets, komplexe Dienstleistungsverträge und stellst die technische Betriebsbereitschaft in einem absoluten High Stakes Umfeld sicher.</p> <p><iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/G6g5dMpRNsc" width="560" height="314"></iframe></p> <h2><strong>Das erwartet dich&nbsp;</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Verantwortung: </strong>Du trägst die alleinige Verantwortung für den technischen Zustand und die Betriebssicherheit des automatisierten FCs. Du überbrückst die Lücke zwischen TGA und Logistikprozessen.</li> <li><strong>Stakeholdermanagement: </strong>Du bist die primäre strategische Ansprechperson für die Standortleitung und agierst auf Augenhöhe mit dem Automation &amp; Engineering Leadership.</li> <li><strong>Krisenmanagement: </strong>Bei kritischen Systemausfällen behältst du den Überblick, koordinierst hochspezialisierte Dienstleistende unter massivem Zeitdruck und erstellst messerscharfe Root Cause Analysen.</li> <li><strong>Budgetpflege:</strong> Du leitest hochkomplexe, großvolumige technische Projekte (CAPEX/OPEX) und steuerst spezialisierte Verträge (z.B. für hochentwickelte Kühl- und IoT-Systeme).</li> <li><strong>Innovation:</strong> Du nutzt fortschrittliche Datenmodelle sowie IoT-Infrastrukturtools, um systemische Probleme proaktiv zu lösen und netzwerkweite Innovationen voranzutreiben.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Das bringst du mit</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Ein abgeschlossenes Studium (Bachelor oder Master) in Facility Management, Gebäudetechnik, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen oder einem vergleichbaren technischen Bereich.</li> <li>5–7 Jahre fundierte Berufserfahrung im technischen Facility Management, idealerweise in der Betreuung von hochautomatisierten Logistikzentren (z. B. mit TGW-, Dematic- oder Vanderlande-Systemen).</li> <li>Fließende Deutsch-, sehr gute Englischkenntnisse und ein Führerschein der Klasse B.</li> <li>Konzeptionelles, abstraktes Denkvermögen auf Makroebene gepaart mit der Fähigkeit, komplexe technische Anforderungen in klare operative Schritte zu übersetzen.</li> <li>Eine starke Act-like-an-Owner-Mentalität. Du setzt außergewöhnlich hohe technische Standards und verteidigst FM-Anforderungen auch unter operativem Druck.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Darauf kannst du dich freuen</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Starte mit uns durch:</strong> Werde Teil unseres internationalen Teams in einem Umfeld, das echtes Wachstum und eine „Act like an Owner“-Mentalität fördert. Treibe Projekte eigenständig voran, teste neue Ideen und profitiere von internen Lern- &amp; Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten durch spannende Workshops und intensive Bootcamps, um deine Skills ständig zu erweitern.</li> <li><strong>Verpflegung:</strong> Genieße jeden Tag ein frisches, kostenloses Frühstück, Mittag- und Abendessen in unseren Standorten, dazu gibt es reichlich Snac

jobs.title: Graduate Operations Supervisor (m/w/d)
jobs.description: <h2><strong>Kurz und knapp</strong></h2> <p>Du hast dein Studium frisch in der Tasche, sprühst vor Tatendrang und willst nicht an der Seitenlinie stehen, sondern direkt das Steuer übernehmen?<br><br>Bei uns steigst du nicht einfach nur ein – du übernimmst ab Tag 1 echte Führungsverantwortung. Als Graduate Operations Supervisor (m/w/d) bist du das pulsierende Herz unseres vollautomatisierten Fulfillment Centers (FC) in&nbsp;<strong>Oberhausen</strong>. Zusammen mit Investoren wie der <em>Bill &amp; Melinda Gates Foundation</em> revolutionieren wir den Markt und bauen das modernste, 100 % elektrische Liefersystem Europas.<br><br><iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/erdeY5trkMA" width="560" height="314"></iframe></p> <h2><strong>Das erwartet dich&nbsp;</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Teamführung: </strong>Du bist Coach, Vorbild und Sparringspartner. Mit echter Empathie führst, inspirierst und entwickelst du dein Team aus 5 Teamleitenden und über 200 Lagermitarbeitenden.</li> <li><strong>Schichtleitung: </strong>Bei dir laufen die Fäden zusammen. Du priorisierst im laufenden Betrieb, löst Engpässe direkt vor Ort und sorgst dafür, dass jede Bestellung pünktlich vom Band rollt.</li> <li><strong>Prozessoptimierung:</strong> Stillstand gibt es nicht. Du blickst über den Tellerrand, zerlegst komplexe Logistikprozesse datenbasiert in ihre Einzelteile und hebst unsere Abläufe mit deinen eigenen Projekten aufs nächste Level.</li> <li><strong>Abwechslung: </strong>Langeweile? Fehlanzeige. Du liebst die Dynamik aus Action direkt auf der Lagerfläche (3-4 Tage pro Woche) und konzeptioneller Deep Dive Arbeit im FC Office (1-2 Tage pro Woche).</li> <li><strong>Stakeholdermanagement: </strong>Wenn der Betrieb kocht, läufst du zur Hochform auf. Du behältst selbst bei ungeplanten Spitzen einen kühlen Kopf, triffst souverän Entscheidungen und gibst deinem Team jederzeit Rückhalt.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Das bringst du mit</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Ein abgeschlossenes Studium (Bachelor oder Master) in Logistik, Supply Chain Management, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen oder einem vergleichbaren Fachbereich.</li> <li>Erste praktische Einblicke in die Lager-, Logistik- oder Produktionswelt (z. B. durch Praktika oder Werkstudententätigkeiten) und absolute Machermentalität.</li> <li>Ein großes Herz für Menschen: Du bist nahbar, kommunizierst sicher auf Deutsch &amp; Englisch und hast Spaß daran, andere über sich hinauswachsen zu lassen.</li> <li>Echte Stressresistenz sowie die nötige Flexibilität für unser rotierendes 3-Schicht-System (6:00 – 14:30 Uhr, 14:30 – 23:00 Uhr &amp; 21:30 – 6:00 Uhr, auch samstags).</li> <li>Einen scharfen, analytischen Verstand, gepaart mit dem unbedingten Willen, Dinge anzupacken und ins Ziel zu bringen.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Darauf kannst du dich freuen</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Starte durch - mit uns:</strong> Werde Teil unseres internationalen Teams in einem Umfeld, das echtes Wachstum und eine „Act like an Owner“-Mentalität fördert. Bei uns hast du die Chance, Projekte eigenverantwortlich voranzutreiben, neue Ideen zu testen und direkt miterleben zu können, wie deine Arbeit in unserem schnell wachsenden Unternehmen Wirkung zeigt.</li> <li><strong>Nachhaltigkeit als Kern:</strong> Werde Teil der Revolution. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description: Filiz est une startup SaaS de 30 personnes qui digitalise aujourd'hui les contrats d'apprentissage en France et construit son deuxième produit : un ERP nouvelle génération pour transformer la façon dont les établissements d'enseignement supérieur opèrent au quotidien. Depuis 2025, Filiz est accompagnée par Hexa, le startup studio français derrière des succès de licornes comme Spendesk, Aircall et Front. Nous attaquons un marché immense, encore largement à réinventer. Le premier produit est en production, les clients sont là. Maintenant, nous entrons dans une nouvelle phase : construire un produit ambitieux, sortir de France et bâtir la référence européenne des outils pour l'enseignement supérieur. Nous cherchons un(e) Senior Software Engineer capable de prendre l'ownership d'un produit, d'une architecture et d'un domaine technique, tout en restant profondément hands-on. Le poste n'a pas de management hiérarchique : ton impact passe par le code, les choix d'architecture et la montée en compétence de l'équipe. Intégré au sein d’une équipe, tu travailleras principalement sur l'ERP, encore en construction : tu participeras à le concevoir et à l'amener jusqu'à la production. Le produit historique reste en production et l'équipe continue de le faire vivre. Ce que tu vas faire chez nous Build & Run de A à Z : tu conçois et fais évoluer des features end-to-end : design, développement, releases et suivi en production. Hands-on & design : tu codes, refactores et améliores l'existant. Tu participes à l'architecture avec le CTO et poses les bases d'un système capable de scaler. PR review & excellence technique : tu élèves le niveau de l'équipe en challengeant le code, la modélisation, les cas limites et la maintenabilité. Intégrations robustes : tu construis des APIs et des systèmes résilients adaptés à des contraintes métier fortes. Fiabilité & observabilité : tu conçois des systèmes capables de détecter et prévenir les problèmes avant qu'ils n'atteignent les utilisateurs. Leadership technique : tu accompagnes les développeurs de l'équipe, partages tes pratiques et fais grandir les personnes autour de toi. Ce qui t'attend techniquement Stack : TypeScript, Next.js, NestJS, MongoDB, Redis, AWS, monorepo Turborepo Observabilité : Sentry, BetterStack, OpenTelemetry Façon de travailler : Kanban, sans sprint. On livre en petits incréments et on deploy plusieurs fois par jour Profil recherché 6+ ans d'expérience avec une expérience prouvée sur des produits en production utilisés par de vrais utilisateurs. Tu as déjà construit et opéré un backend dans la durée. Tu connais les compromis d'une architecture qui doit tenir dans le temps. Tu es capable de couvrir tout le cycle : compréhension du produit, system design, développement, déploiement et run. Tu as le réflexe des cas limites. Quand on manipule des documents légaux et des données dont nos clients dépendent au quotidien, la question « que se passe-t-il si cet appel échoue au milieu ? » compte plus que la maîtrise d'un framework. Tu sais prendre des décisions avec une information incomplète et les assumer. On cherche quelqu'un qui tranche, pas quelqu'un qui organise une quatrième réunion. Tu sais avancer dans l'imparfait. La dette technique existe, elle est nommée et priorisée : tu préfères faire progresser le produit plutôt que de viser une perfection théorique. Tu utilises l'IA au quotidien et tu veux participer à construire nos pratiques et nos outils, pas seulement coder plus vite. Tu as déjà joué un rôle de Tech Lead : ownership d'un système, décisions d'architecture et accompagnement d'autres développeurs. Processus de recrutement Echange RH Entretien technique avec un développeur de l'équipe Entretien technique (algorithme et design technique) avec le CTO Entretien de fit avec deux des fondateurs Prise de référence et offre Conditions Salaire : 50-65 k€ selon expérience Télétravail : full remote (et des bureaux à Paris si tu en as envie) Find more English Speaking Jobs

jobs.description: The opportunity Tax advisory has everything automation needs: structured data, recurring work, clear rules. Yet the profession never made the leap, because recurring does not mean uniform. Every case has its own twist, and the law keeps moving. Reasoning resolves exactly this variance. That is why the window is open now. The model is no longer the scarce part. Expert knowledge and real case data are, and AI labs pay a premium for exactly this. Vogel holds what no AI-native player has: decades of accounting data, edge cases and judgment calls from several thousand mid-sized companies, audited and closed. It never leaves the house, and it becomes the edge of what you build. The market is being reordered: four in ten tax advisors in Germany leave the profession within ten years, and many of their firms will find no successor. Vogel acquires established advisory firms and develops them further, and every acquisition adds to that base. We have already produced our own annual financial statements with AI. Today, that is one person with a tool. Turning it into a capability of the whole company is the job. You own the technology that makes Vogel AI-first: the data layer above DATEV, the agent infrastructure on top, and the control layer without which nothing in this profession may go live. You decide the architecture and the stack of what we build. What it does and in which order is decided together with Operations and Moritz Vogel in the role of chief product officer, close to the advisors who use it; you shape it with them. You report to and work directly with Moritz Vogel. What you'll do Architecture above DATEV Build the data layer above DATEV. DATEV stays the system of record (for now); the value is created in the layer above it, designed to outlive the system beneath. Choose and build the agent infrastructure: framework, orchestration, versioning, observability. You answer these questions with code, not with a slide deck. Make integration a capability, not a project: every client brings their own upstream systems, and today each connection is built by hand. Build the layer those systems plug into, so what makes a client different arrives as context the agents read, never as custom code. One more client must never mean one more integration project. Reproducibility and control A tax advisor must get the same result twice, and an auditor must be able to trace it. Probabilistic where there is variance, deterministic where there are numbers. Build the control layer so that a certified professional sees within seconds what an agent did (version, source, decision) and can sign off on it. Build evaluation on decades of audited, completed work. Team and scale Make the architecture calls: design, stack, build or buy for the layer. Nobody has decided it for you, and nobody will overrule it by committee. Hire and lead the engineering team. The budget for your first engineers is approved. You start hiring in your first quarter. Make every acquired firm land on the same base, so technology scales with every acquisition. And stay in the code: you commit and you review. Questions you'll answer Where exactly does probabilistic end and deterministic begin? How does a system learn from closed cases without losing its reproducibility? A new client arrives with their own systems. What may change in the system, and what may not? What success looks like 6 months: Architecture decided. One real use case from the core business runs in production and is used daily. Your first engineers are hired. 12 months: Several agentic use cases in regular operation. The control layer holds up in a real review, and evaluation runs against closed cases, not test data. 24 months: Automation is a capability of the organization, not of individuals. Every acquired firm runs on the same base, and your team ships without you in the room. Where it leads: the full CTO mandate, a management career earned by contribution, not by years served. jobs.description: About us Launched in 2019, Constructor is an AI-first e-commerce search and discovery platform that helps shoppers find the right products at the right time and enables leading global e-commerce brands to drive meaningful revenue and conversion gains. About the team The SABR team owns the top layer of request processing for product discovery. We own the service that first receives product discovery requests (autocomplete, search, browse & recommendations) & executes the entire business logic that drives product discovery. That service also functions as a gateway to parse incoming user requests, orchestrate calls across the internal services that do the ranking and retrieval, interpret their responses, and assemble the final response the customer sees. We also own the public configuration APIs customers use to control how discovery behaves, and the MCP layer that exposes all of it to AI agents. Our team owns both platform & product components: Because of the positioning of our services, we take part in every architectural decision of our core product offering. At the same time, our goals are heavily influenced by direct customer feedback, because all product discovery-related features are either implemented in or integrated with our services. All of our services are public APIs, so interface design and backward compatibility are a constant part of the job. But most of our attention goes to keeping them fast and up: we serve up to 15k RPS, fan out to many internal services on every request, and are expected to stay available and degrade gracefully when any of them fails or slows down. The work is distributed systems in practice rather than in theory: request orchestration, failure isolation, caching, latency budgets, capacity planning, and the observability to know what is actually happening in production. The team is small enough that engineers own problems end to end, from design through on-call. About you You're a senior engineer who wants to own features end to end, not just close tickets. What we are looking for Technical Solid experience building and operating backend services in production, ideally high-traffic or low-latency ones. Extensive Python knowledge (our primary language). Hands-on experience with observability (metrics, logs, traces) and debugging performance issues in live systems. Experience designing and evolving public APIs that external customers depend on. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing. Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday. Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on. An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you. Still unsure about why joining us? You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before. jobs.title: Data analyst - AML
jobs.description: About the team: At SumUp, keeping our platform safe and compliant is critical to the trust of the millions of small businesses we serve around the world. You'll join our Global AML team at an exciting point in its growth. We're expanding into new markets, evolving our AML capabilities, introducing AI-enabled controls, and navigating increasingly complex regulatory expectations. As an AML Data Analyst, you'll play a key role in turning AML data into actionable insights. Working closely with our global AML Operations and AML Governance teams, as well as colleagues across Engineering and Data, you'll help us understand how our controls are performing, identify risks and gaps early, and make better decisions as our business scales. This is a role where your analysis will go beyond reporting. The insights you generate will directly support how we monitor, improve, and strengthen our global AML framework.   What you'll do: Build and maintain AML dashboards, operational reports, and data packs used by AML Operations, AML Governance, and senior leadership Design measurement frameworks that track AML operational KPIs, including case volumes, productivity, SLA adherence, and screening hit rates Support AML teams by providing data extracts, analysis, trend identification, and root-cause analysis on AML control outputs and data quality issues Run data validation and quality checks to keep AML data accurate and consistent across systems and regions Support Transaction Monitoring and Sanctions/PEP screening through data analysis, requirements definition, and testing Partner with Engineering and AML Operations to define data requirements and support automation projects Build self-service analytics resources so AML Operations teams can explore data and find insights independently   You'll be great for this role if you have: Experience in data analytics, business intelligence, or a similar role within financial services, fintech, compliance, AML, or another regulated environment. Strong SQL skills, including writing complex queries and building reliable datasets for reporting and analysis. Practical experience with Python for data analysis and automation. Experience working with a cloud data warehouse such as Snowflake. Strong analytical skills, with the ability to identify patterns, trends, root causes, and actionable insights from complex data. The ability to translate technical analysis into clear recommendations and stories for non-technical stakeholders and senior leaders. Experience working with data quality, validation, multiple data sources, and competing stakeholder priorities. A proactive, curious mindset and interest in AML, financial crime, fintech, and emerging technologies such as AI, with the ability to take ownership in a fast-changing environment.   Why you should join SumUp: 🌍 Opportunity to work with SumUppers globally on large-scale fintech products used by millions of businesses worldwide, from our Berlin office. jobs.title: Implementation Manager DACH
jobs.description: Build with us Businesses deserve better from finance. Less friction, more freedom. Since 2004, Mollie has been on a mission to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe. Today, more than 250,000 companies trust our all-in-one platform to get paid, manage money and grow on their terms. Simple, scalable and built with real businesses in mind. We're one of Europe's fastest-growing fintechs, with 950+ Mollies across 14+ locations. Our people make this growth possible. We move fast, build with purpose and care deeply about our customers. Whether you're solving problems, building market-leading products or exploring how AI can make work smarter, you'll have the freedom to create and the trust to deliver. If you're ready to grow, shape the future of fintech and join an ambitious, high-performing team, this is the place for you. Your impact As Implementation Manager, you'll own the post-sales integration phase for Mollie's largest and most complex deals, guiding merchants from handover through testing to go live. You'll run kickoffs with internal and external stakeholders, set go live dates, keep progress on track, and coordinate testing and feedback along the way. You'll work closely with colleagues across sales, product and engineering, as well as with merchants directly, keeping everyone aligned as deals move toward launch. jobs.title: Prevention Analyst - Pentesting
jobs.description: Prevention Analyst - Pentesting About this role We are looking for a Prevention Analyst - Pentester, to join our Prevention track. An attacker does not look at one server in isolation. They look at everything a company exposes to the internet and work out where to start. You will do the same for our clients, taking the attacker’s view of their external attack surface, seeing what an attacker sees, and doing what an attacker would do next. That means reading the story behind an attack surface. A forgotten subdomain, an old login portal, and a misconfigured mail server may each look minor on their own. Together they can show how an organisation has grown, where its blind spots are, and where someone could get in. When you find a potential weak point, you dig into it technically to find out how far an attacker could actually go. This is not a classic penetration testing role. The deep dive draws on pentest methodology and expertise, but it is not a full pentest, and you will not spend your weeks writing long reports. We focus on finding the high impact vulnerabilities that need attention now and getting them to the client in a form they can act on. This is for someone with hands on pentesting experience who wants to work across many customer environments, sharpen their attacker mindset, and grow into owning complex prevention engagements end to end. What you will do Assess clients’ external attack surface as a whole, from the attacker’s perspective. Identify gaps and weaknesses across the surface, not just within a single asset, and work out how they connect. Run technical deep dives into potential weak points to establish how far an attacker could get in practice. Separate what needs fixing now from what does not, and focus on high and critical findings with immediate impact. Turn technical findings into short, clear advice that clients can understand and act on. Share what you learn with the team and actively pick up what others know. We work on problems together. Contribute to improving our approach, sharing ideas that make assessments faster, clearer, and more useful for clients. What you will need Hands on penetration testing experience and a solid grasp of pentest methodology, particularly for external infrastructure and web applications. The ability to think like an attacker, to look at a set of exposed assets and see where you would start and why. Good judgement about real world impact, so you can tell an interesting finding from an urgent one. The ability to explain technical findings to non technical readers, briefly and without losing accuracy. A collaborative way of working and a genuine interest in learning and growing with colleagues, not working as a solo player. Comfortable working across multiple client environments in parallel. Fluent English. Nice-to-have Certifications such as OSCP, BSCP, or CPTS. A proven bug bounty track record or other real world offensive security experience. Experience working with SMEs or mid market customers on security topics. What we offer A meaningful mission, protecting organisations across Europe from real world cyber threats. Work with top tier professionals from national CERTs, intelligence agencies, and leading tech backgrounds. A remote friendly culture with quarterly meetups and annual company retreats, for example in Spain, Portugal, or Italy. Thursday socials to stay connected. A generous time off policy, including wellbeing and volunteering days. We combine cutting edge technology with hands on expertise to detect, respond to, and recover from cyber threats in real time. Your main focus will be on R&D and will involve building and showcasing a demonstrator that utilizes industrial robot arms to automate currently manual tasks. Work with industry-standard hardware platforms (e.g., ROS-compatible robots, specific sensor suites) to develop and deploy robotic manipulators for real world testing. Design advanced planning algorithms to optimize manipulation tasks such as pick-and-place operations. Previously trained RL models in both simulated and real-world environments with continuous action and state spaces. jobs.title: Senior People Partner
jobs.description: Senior People Partner Cloudscaler | London | People Team | Reports to the Chief People Officer | £55,000–£75,000 Someone has to own the People initiative that doesn’t fit neatly into anyone’s week and the case nobody else should be handling. That someone is you — not as an escalation point, but as the person who runs the day-to-day of this function. THE MOMENT Cloudscaler is 130 people today. We’ll be 170 by the end of this year, and roughly double again in 2027. The People function is being built in real time alongside that growth, rather than inherited from someone who left years ago. You’ll be the first hire into the People team. For roughly your first year you’ll be the only People professional alongside the CPO, which means running the whole day-to-day of the function: the hardest casework and initiatives, and the operational core that keeps everything moving. A People Partner is planned to join later in 2027, and at that point the operational administration moves to them. This is also a role built with room to grow. As the team expands beyond that second hire, we expect this role to take on day-to-day operational leadership of the People Partner practice, but that isn’t the shape of it on day one. WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT In most People teams, the senior generalist is just a People Partner with a harder case queue. Here, the difference is ownership, not just difficulty. Complex casework: Rather than simply handling harder cases, you’ll own the most complex cases end to end, with no hand back. People initiatives: Rather than contributing to initiatives someone else drives, you’ll own them from design through to embedding. Decision-making: Rather than escalating ambiguity upward, you’ll make the sensible call and document your reasoning. CPO partnership: Rather than acting in a support role to the CPO, you’ll be an operational partner they can confidently delegate to. To be clear about the level: The CPO still designs the People strategy and the systems architecture. You own how it runs day to day, and you’re trusted to run a whole initiative, not just a case. That is a different job to People Partner, not a bigger version of the same one. THE ROLE You’ll sit in the People team reporting to the Chief People Officer. Three strands make up the job: Casework: The employee relations situations with the most complexity or sensitivity land with you, start to finish. Initiatives: When the CPO needs a piece of work owned (a policy rollout, a wellbeing programme, a piece of the reward or benefits agenda), you take it from design through to something that runs. Operations: Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own payroll and benefits administration, onboarding, screening and security clearances, and keeping Rippling accurate. When the People Partner joins, they’ll report to the CPO. You won’t manage them formally, but you’ll lead their handover, you’ll be the person they come to first, and your judgement will set the standard for how this function operates day to day. WHERE THE ROLE STARTS AND STOPS New roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today. Yours The most complex and sensitive employee relations casework, end to end. Full ownership of People initiatives, from design to embedding. Acting as the CPO’s operational partner on ambiguous or cross-cutting problems. Once the People Partner joins: A structured handover of the operational core. Day-to-day guidance for the People Partner. Shared Ashby, which Talent Acquisition owns. jobs.description: About Lendable Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start: One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK Profitable since 2017 Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot ) So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance . We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days. We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes. Join us if you want to Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1 Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions Build the best technology in-house : we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting About the Role Lendable is a high-growth FinTech building its security operations capability deliberately. As a Senior Security Operations Analyst, you will triage and respond to security alerts, help improve the quality of the detections behind them, and lead the response when a security event becomes an incident. You will investigate alerts and escalations from our MSSP, tune our monitoring so that it finds more of what matters and less of what doesn’t, and act as a trusted Incident Commander for security incidents, from declaration through to post-incident review. You will work with Engineering, IT, Legal, Risk and senior stakeholders, and you will be credible with all of them. Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology. AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen. About Frontier Faculty Frontier™ is a decision operating system. It puts AI to work on the decisions that matter most to large organisations, such as where to invest, how to allocate resources, and when to act. Every enterprise is investing heavily in AI, but few are confident it will improve performance. Too often it goes to what’s easy to automate, disconnected from the decisions that actually move the business. Frontier works backwards from objectives like revenue, margin and risk to the decisions that drive them, then connects the data, models and agents those decisions need into a world model of the business. Teams simulate and optimise options with ADA, our AI decision agent, and every decision is tracked against its outcome so the system keeps learning. Our ambition is to make business decisions as easy to navigate as getting around a city. We don’t believe in AI that thinks for people. We believe in AI that helps people think, with humans and agents working together inside a decision system. Customers start with one high-value decision and prove value in weeks. Over months they connect it into a wider decision network, and over years they build an adaptive enterprise. Frontier is built by Faculty, an AI company that has delivered more than 400 systems since 2014 and is now part of Accenture. About Design at Frontier We’re a small team, growing deliberately - we’d rather have five designers who trust each other than fifteen who don't. We're tightly integrated with engineering. We prototype in code. We co-own the design system with developers. We're actively exploring what agentic-augmented design work looks like in practice, not in think pieces — and we're honest when we don't have the answer yet. We’re active in shaping the product culture at Frontier; putting people first, raising the quality bar and ensuring a coherent experience. You’ll be part of shaping that culture. About the role You'll be one of the most senior designers on Frontier, shaping a product that's still early enough that the decisions you make will define how it works for years. Day to day, you'll be designing the surfaces where people and agents collaborate on real clinical decisions — how evidence gets surfaced, how recommendations get explained, how humans push back, how teams learn. This is hard, unsolved design work. The existing patterns for AI interfaces mostly come from consumer chat products; they don't transfer cleanly to environments where the cost of a bad decision is measured in years of research or patient outcomes. jobs.title: KYC/KYB Analyst
jobs.description: [OUR MISSION AND CUSTOMERS] We are creating the freedom for SMEs to succeed by delivering Europe's leading finance workspace with banking at its core, augmented by financial tools. We are proud to be rated 4.7 on Trustpilot, based on 60,000 reviews. Our culture puts customer satisfaction at the core of what we do (more about our culture here ). [OUR JOURNEY] Founded in 2016 and launched in 2017 by Alexandre and Steve , Qonto has grown to 1,700 Qontoers serving over 750,000 customers across 8 European countries. We have been profitable since 2023, and we are just getting started. [OUR BELIEFS] We hire for skills and potential. With 80+ nationalities, 45% women, and 56% of women in our leadership team, diversity isn't a program; It's who we are. We've built a discrimination-free hiring process because the best teams are built on merit. [AI AT QONTO] AI is deeply embedded in how we work ( here ) - Every Qontoer gets unlimited access to the best AI tools. We want people who experiment without waiting for permission, push AI beyond the obvious, know when to trust it, and when to question it. Join us as a KYC/KYB Analyst to protect Qonto's regulated growth while keeping onboarding fast and fair for our clients. You'll review enhanced due diligence and KYBC cases, decide who can safely open or keep a Qonto account, and flag financial-crime risks the moment you spot them, working closely with our Lead EDD. ➡️ What you'll do Decide on high-risk files: Review EDD cases for onboarding and lifecycle reviews, then approve, reject, or send them back to L1 for missing or invalid documents. Handle KYBC edge cases fast: Assess alternative documents and gray-activity requests, closing decisions within a 48-hour SLA when clients are blocked. Focus where it matters: Automation handles the routine files, so you'll concentrate your judgment on the riskiest ones during your weekly control checks. Cross-check the numbers: Compare declared turnover and financial documentation against real account activity to spot inconsistencies. ➡️ What we're looking for Fluent in French and English, including legal reading: You read bylaws, RCS extracts, and legal documentation as comfortably as any other business document, in French, and work just as easily in English. Risk judgment under ambiguity: You reason through gray-area cases instead of defaulting to blanket rejection or blanket approval. AFC/KYC/KYB fundamentals: You're curious about AFC/KYC/KYB topics and ready to learn on the job. Attention to detail: You catch missing documents, invalid evidence, and inconsistencies that others might miss. AI-native mindset: You're comfortable letting AI handle routine cases so you can focus on the ones that need real judgment. ➡️ What we can offer you Real autonomy, fast: Reach independent decision-making on routine files within a few months, with complex cases escalated together. A growing scope: As Qonto's credit products expand, you'll take on larger companies and more complex corporate structures over time. Structured onboarding: Shadow the team, get weekly 1:1s, and have every early decision reviewed before you go fully autonomous. A seat at the intersection of compliance and fraud: Your work directly feeds AFCU's transaction-monitoring investigations, broadening your view beyond onboarding. [DIVERSITY] At Qonto, we understand that true diversity isn’t just about ticking boxes on a hiring checklist. Apply regardless of the boxes you tick - who knows? You may have the missing piece of the puzzle we’ve been searching for all along. [HIRING PROCESS DURATION] On average, our hiring process lasts 20 working days. More information on our candidate journey here [DATA RETENTION] By applying, you agree that Qonto processes your personal data to assess your application. Your data is kept for up to 2 years in our candidate pool. Read our Privacy Notice for full details. 🔒 Your security matters to us Recruitment scams are on the rise. jobs.title: Business Line Manager - Money Flows
jobs.description: About Ledger We’re a team of experts pushing the limits of what’s possible, united by our common goal to unlock true freedom through digital ownership, making technology accessible for all. We believe in a world where users, creators and enterprises manage their value with ownership and freedom. Our curiosity drives us to innovate, empowering individuals on a global scale. We believe change is constant and our team moves forward as one, with a culture of problem-solving where every employee is empowered and supported to challenge tradition and create solutions. Our mission is simple: to make self-custody accessible and give people the keys to their own financial futures. If you want to make a true impact, we want you to join us at Ledger. At Ledger, we’re proud to be the global platform for digital assets and Web3, with over 20% of the world’s crypto assets secured through our Ledger devices. With our headquarters in Paris, and offices in Vierzon, Grenoble, Montpellier, London, Portland, Geneva, Zurich and Central Singapore, we have a team of around 600 professionals developing a variety of products and services to enable individuals and companies to securely buy, store, swap, grow and manage crypto assets – including the Ledger hardware wallets line with more than 7.5 millions units already sold in 200 countries. The team: With over 8 million signers sold worldwide, Ledger Wallet is where Ledger users manage and grow their assets. Transactional Services (buy, sell, swap, trading and stablecoin products) is its main source of service revenue. Money Flows connects users' crypto to the fiat world in both directions: on/off-ramp , cash-to-stablecoin , Card , and the growing P2P and Payments use cases. Users buy crypto with fiat or sell it back to their bank, move cash into stablecoins, and spend crypto with a card, all through specialist partners. It is the entry and exit door of the Ledger Wallet economy and a key lever to diversify Transactional Services revenue. The role reports to the Senior Director, Transactional Services. What you’ll be doing: You own and grow Money Flows end to end - revenue, economics, partner ecosystem and the quality of every fiat journey in Ledger Wallet - with a General Manager mindset over a business run mostly through external partners and cross-functional teams. The ambition is to grow revenue 10x in two to three years, through a strategy and roadmap you define and turn into quantified milestones. Key responsibilities include: Business Line Ownership & Revenue Delivery: Being ultimately accountable for Money Flows revenue, volume and take rate across buy, sell, cash-to-stablecoin, Card, P2P and Payments. Building and defending the forecast, querying the data yourself, and separating market effects from the levers the team controls. Monetization & Pricing: Owning take rate by line, partner and payment method. Turning volume into direct or indirect revenue (zero-fee partners, cash-to-stablecoin flows), and keeping pricing/product competitive against exchanges, neobanks and other wallets. Partner Management & Business Development: Identifying, signing, managing and negotiating with the ramp, payment, stablecoin and card-issuing partner bench - on pricing, geographic and payment-method coverage, conversion, KYC friction and operational quality. Managing concentration risk, onboarding new providers to close gaps, and running a monthly review with each partner. Card Programme Ownership: Running the card programme: economics, activation and dormancy, issuer and processor performance, card-scheme negotiations (including geo expansion), and the go-to-market with Marketing. Ledger Wallet Experience: Working with the Product Line Manager to improve the Buy, Sell, Card and Pay journeys, and making sure every release ships with a coordinated go-to-market. Stablecoin & Payments Roadmap: Shaping how Ledger captures stablecoin and payment use cases - cash-to-stablecoin, Pay and peer-to-peer flows
