jobs.title: Senior Growth Product Manager
jobs.description: Data quality is the bottleneck of the AI era. Every Fortune 500 is trying to solve it. We're the team they call. Soda is the data quality layer for Disney, Ralph Lauren, CBRE, HelloFresh, 2K Games, and Nubank. Our open-source engine, Soda Core, is used by companies like Tesla, Slack, Adyen, Walmart, and JPMC. The category is growing fast because AI doesn't work on bad data, and we're hiring a Senior Growth Product Manager to get customers using Soda faster and on more of their data. About Us Soda's mission is to monitor the world's decisions. We're building the first Data & AI performance monitoring platform that spans data collection to automated decision-making. Soda helps customers find, understand, and fix data quality issues by combining automated post-production monitoring with pre-production pipeline data testing. Soda was founded in 2019 by Maarten (employee #5 at Collibra) and Tom (creator of multiple open-source projects generating hundreds of millions in value). We commercialize through Soda Cloud and we're well-funded, with investors like Point 9 Capital, Hummingbird, Singular, and Eurazeo. The Role You'll lead our adoption team, a small group of frontend, full-stack, and AI engineers. The team works on onboarding and activation, on keeping workflows coherent across the product, on customer-facing dashboards, and on AI features that save users work. Most of our roadmap is driven by what customers and prospects ask for. This team's work is driven by adoption metrics, because customers rarely ask for the things that would make them use Soda more. You'll start from a hypothesis, for example that changing a flow will get 20% more data contracts created, ship the change, and check whether it worked. We sell to enterprises, so sample sizes are small and A/B tests rarely reach significance. You'll use product analytics, session replays, and conversations with users, and you'll often have to decide with incomplete data. This is a product role. If most of your growth experience is in paid acquisition or lifecycle email, it's probably the wrong fit. You'll also work closely with our Growth team, which is led by a co-founder, on launches and messaging. What You'll Do Own the adoption metrics for Soda Cloud: time to first verified contract for new accounts, data coverage (datasets with contracts and monitors), weekly active datasets and users, and usage of AI features. You'll define them, make sure we can measure them, and improve them. Own the UX of workflows across the product and keep them coherent for our two kinds of users: data engineers, and business users such as data stewards and governance leads. Find where customers get stuck between signing the contract and running Soda on most of their data, and decide what to fix first. Design and ship onboarding flows that get a new team to first value within days, including self-serve paths for technical teams that want to evaluate Soda on their own. Put AI to work on adoption: decide which steps an agent should do for the user, ship them with the team, and measure whether people keep using them. Work with Growth on launches and product marketing, and with our customer engineers on whatever is blocking rollouts at customers. Hiring Process Application: your CV, plus a short answer about one metric you moved (what it was, what you shipped, what happened, and what didn't work) 15-minute phone screen First interview (60 min): a deep dive into product growth work you've done. Part of it is showing us something you shipped that you'd still be proud to demo. Second interview (60 min): a working session on a real Soda adoption problem Culture fit (45 min) We answer every application, and every candidate hears back within 3–5 days of each step. If it's not a hell yes, it's a no, and we'll tell you quickly and kindly. Requirements You Should Have 5+ years in product, including at least 2 owning growth, activation, onboarding, or adoption in B2B SaaS : you were accountable for a metr

Today, more than 12,000 brands use Vibe.co to reach 120 million+ households. And in August 2026, Vibe.co became a Walmart company, opening up a new chapter for the business and the industry. With Walmart’s first-party data and purchase signals now part of the Vibe platform, advertisers can connect TV advertising to real-world transactions and measure the impact of CTV with a level of precision previously associated with platforms like Google and Meta. This is a unique moment to join Vibe. With Walmart’s scale, data, and reach behind us, we’re building the next generation of TV advertising and creating a more measurable, performance-driven future for the channel. Your team You will join the Supply team, which owns Vibe's inventory: the publishers we partner with, the deals we run, and the catalog of apps, channels and shows our advertisers care about. Shows are the reason people turn on their TV. Advertisers don't just want impressions: they want to show up next to the right shows, live sports and premium channels. Supply brings that content to Vibe through direct publisher partnerships, curated deals and sponsorships. It makes it easy to find, understand and buy, through real-time bidding, or any technology the publisher uses. Premium publishers care as much about which ads run on their shows as about who buys them, and great creatives are what earn us access. The team brings together partnerships, operations, and product. You will work closely with the DSP team, which runs the bidding infrastructure, and the Performance team, which decides how to value each opportunity, as well as with publisher partners directly. Your mission As a Senior Software Engineer on Supply, you will build the systems that let Vibe grow, operate, and trust its inventory. You will turn publisher partnerships into live, healthy supply, and give the business and our partners the tools to manage it at scale. What you will do Publisher integrations Build and improve publisher integrations end-to-end, from onboarding a new partner to supporting new ad formats and sponsorship offers. Implement measurement requirements with publishers and the DSP team (e.g. UID2, publisher IDs) so the bidder sees richer inventory. Own integration health: detect broken or degraded supply before it costs us spend. Automate the routine work of the Supply team (new deals, stale-supply cleanup, troubleshooting) so it scales with the number of partners, and with Vibe. Supply tooling & publisher platform Build real-time monitoring, alerting, and analytics on supply volume, quality, and spend. Build publisher-facing features: reporting, insights, and self-serve catalog tools. jobs.title: Senior Full-Stack Product Engineer
jobs.description: About Us Base360.ai is the AI operating system for short-term rental businesses, helping property managers run their operations on autopilot. Born out of The Flex, a short-term rental operator that scaled to an eight-figure business using its own software, Base360.ai is now launching as a standalone platform for short-term rental operators worldwide. We bring reservations, guest communication, pricing, payments, cleaning, maintenance, and reporting into one platform—helping operators automate manual work, reduce costs, increase revenue, and scale their portfolios. We're looking for an ambitious Senior Full-Stack Product Engineer who wants to turn real customer problems into intuitive, reliable software. You'll work closely with founders, designers, and operators to identify what matters, build solutions, and improve them based on how people use them. If you enjoy owning the full journey from customer problem to shipped product—and you're excited by AI, automation, and short-term rentals—we want to meet you. What You'll Build As a Senior Full-Stack Product Engineer, you'll help shape and scale Base360.ai across the entire short-term rental lifecycle. You'll build customer-facing features, operational dashboards, automation engines, AI-powered workflows, and integrations that help property managers grow without increasing their workload at the same rate. Your work will connect what users see with the systems behind it—from a guest’s check-in experience to the workflows coordinating reservations, cleaning, payments, and owner reporting. Your Mission Understand Customer Problems Work directly with property managers and internal teams to understand their workflows, identify friction, and decide which problems are worth solving. Build Products End-to-End Take features from idea and prototype through frontend, backend, integrations, testing, and deployment. Own the complete experience and how it performs in production. Create Intuitive User Experiences Work with designers to make complex short-term rental operations easy to manage. Build interfaces that help users complete tasks quickly and confidently. Create Powerful Automations Build event-driven workflows that eliminate repetitive work—from scheduling cleaning after a booking to sending check-in instructions and generating owner statements. Develop AI-Powered Features Use LLMs and AI agents to automate guest communication, triage maintenance requests, support pricing decisions, and help operators manage their portfolios more efficiently. Connect the Ecosystem Build reliable APIs and integrations with platforms including Airbnb, Hostaway, Stripe, Twilio, OpenAI, Google, and other partners across the short-term rental ecosystem. Solve Real Operational Problems Build solutions for: Real-time reservation and availability synchronization Dynamic pricing intelligence Smart lock access and key management Automated guest communication across channels Guest check-in and upsell journeys Operational forecasting Cleaning and maintenance automation Owner reporting and financial workflows AI-powered monitoring and alerts Measure and Improve Use customer feedback, product usage, and operational results to evaluate what you ship. Improve features based on adoption, time saved, fewer errors, and better user outcomes. Build for Scale Make sound technical decisions that balance delivery speed, maintainability, security, and reliability as more operators and properties join the platform. jobs.description: About Alta Ares Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them. cost Work closely with 3D printing operations to define printable geometries, tolerances, post-processing, and qualify parts for flight use Drive a rapid, fail-fast iteration process: build, test, configurations, working with aerostructures and systems teams Apply and enforce design rules for operation in extreme environments (cold and hot climates, rain, humidity, icing conditions) to ensure engine reliability across the full operational envelope Contribute to engine testing (bench and flight), performance validation, and continuous design improvement Candidate Profile: Minimum 8 years of experience in jet engine / gas turbine design, with a proven track record of having designed and delivered engine models (not just component-level work) Strong hands-on experience with small jet turbine/engine components for metal additive manufacturing (DfAM), and practical knowledge of metal 3D printing processes and constraints Comfortable working in a rapid-iteration, fail-fast development culture rather than a traditional long-cycle aerospace process Experience integrating propulsion systems into airframes (flying wing or similar unconventional platforms is a strong plus) Knowledge of design requirements for extreme operating environments (temperature extremes, precipitation, icing) Ability to work autonomously in a small, fast-paced startup team, wearing multiple hats when needed Nice to Have Experience with UAV/drone propulsion specifically (vs. manned aviation) Familiarity with low-cost manufacturing strategies for defense/dual-use hardware Prior startup or We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. The Role As the Vice President of our Production Platform organization, you will own how reliably Mistral runs in production and how fast every Mistral engineer ships. This role combines deep infrastructure expertise with organizational leadership to build a platform that scales ahead of the company. Production Platform brings together around 55 engineers across site reliability, deployment, build and CI, and our internal service framework, led by strong team leads. Every deploy and every model release goes through this organization, from our own cloud to the major hyperscalers, private clouds and our customers’ on-premise environments. You will set the strategy for the organization, grow its leaders and shape the organization as it scales. The role is key to the reliability of our products, the velocity of our engineering and research teams, and our ability to deliver Mistral wherever our customers need it. What You Will Do Lead the Production Platform organization through its Engineering Managers, and grow them as leaders. Set the strategy and roadmap for reliability, deployment, build and CI, and the internal service framework. Own the reliability of our production environment: SLOs, on-call, incident management and capacity. Make delivery to every environment, from SaaS to private cloud and on-premise, as simple and dependable as a single deploy. Raise engineering velocity across the company with fast, trusted CI and safe deployments by default. Give product teams strong defaults and the ownership of their own services and tests. Design the organization as it scales: structure, hiring, on-call models and processes. Contribute to architecture and the hard technical decisions, staying close to the systems. Partner with Product Engineering, Research and our enterprise teams to align the platform with their needs. Define and track the metrics that matter: reliability, delivery speed and developer experience. What We're Looking For Deep background in infrastructure, site reliability or production engineering, starting as a hands-on engineer. Experience leading leaders: managing managers and growing strong team leads. Experience scaling an infrastructure or platform organization through fast growth. Track record of running production systems at scale, with measurable results on reliability or delivery speed. Ability to set strategy in an ambiguous scope and turn it into execution. Strong technical judgment in distributed systems, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure and CI/CD. Experience delivering software into customer environments (on-premise, private cloud, air-gapped) is a strong plus. Experience with AI infrastructure, such as model serving or GPU platforms, is a plus. Low ego, at ease with constant change, and driven by results. jobs.title: ML Hydrologist, Flood Forecasting
jobs.description: About the Role Global ML flood models now outperform traditional approaches on large rivers, but they still break down in the small, fast catchments where flash floods happen. Riverkin, a VC-backed ETH Zürich Spin-off, is closing that gap. We start from hydrological models trained across thousands of catchments worldwide and make them accurate locally, using a sensor network we deploy ourselves in exactly the places public datasets don't reach. We are looking for an ML hydrologist to own that work. You will report to the CTO and work directly with our other hydrologist, who covers rainfall radar and short-term nowcasting. Why this is interesting Data nobody else has: Our own field-deployed sensors give you live streamflow observations in small, previously ungauged catchments. An open problem: Whether large-sample models can be made reliable at flash-flood scale is unsolved, and you would be working on it with real data and real users. Built to protect lives and critical infrastructure: Your models will power early flood warning systems safeguarding hydropower plants and giving first responders more time to protect communities Publishing and open source: We encourage publishing results and contributing to open tools such as NeuralHydrology and Caravan. Compute: GPU resources are available for training and experimentation. What You'll Do Bring global flood models to the local scale Take state-of-the-art hydrological ML models (LSTMs, Transformers) trained on large-sample datasets and adapt them to the catchments our customers care about. Use our own sensor data alongside public gauge, reanalysis and radar data to fine-tune and validate those models locally. Tackle prediction in ungauged and data-scarce basins through transfer learning and regionalisation. Own hydrological modelling end to end: set the technical direction, decide when to adapt pre-trained models or train our own, and lead the work from experimentation through validation to production. Work as one modelling team Make practical trade-offs between forecast accuracy, model complexity and development effort to build a reliable product that meets customer needs. Work side by side with our hydrologist specialising in rainfall radar and nowcasting to directly integrate rainfall nowcasts into your flood models. Work with software engineers to put models into production and monitor their performance. Identify and test advances in ML flood forecasting, turning promising research into more accurate and reliable forecasts for our customers. Stay close to the real world We believe the best modellers understand the world behind their models. We encourage you to join field deployments and customer conversations to build that understanding firsthand. You are an opinionated contributor to key technical decisions. Who You Are You’ve built and validated hydrological ML models across many catchments and have experience taking modelling work into real-world use. You combine scientific rigour with product judgement: you test assumptions, understand uncertainty and focus on improvements that matter to customers. You take ownership from an open question to a working solution. You set priorities, make decisions and keep moving without waiting for perfect information. You care deeply about the quality of your work. You dig into why models fail, follow problems through and stay invested in how your forecasts perform after deployment. You communicate clearly in writing and in person, can explain your reasoning and trade-offs, and work closely with people across hydrology, software, hardware and field operations. Technical Requirements MSc or PhD in hydrology, water resources, or atmospheric sciences . Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning ML streamflow or flood models across many catchments at once (regional, continental or global), for example on CAMELS or Caravan. We’re making conversational shopping a reality, connecting every shopper with tailored guidance and product expertise — available on demand, at every touchpoint in their journey. We're designing the future of autonomous marketing , taking the work out of workflows, and reclaiming the creative, strategic, and customer-first work marketers were always meant to do. Thumbtack is the one app you need to take care of and improve your home — from personalized guidance to AI tools and a best-in-class hiring experience. Every day in every county of the U.S., people turn to Thumbtack to complete urgent repairs, seasonal maintenance and bigger improvements. At Thumbtack, the Applied Science team is responsible for a wide variety of problems spanning AI, machine learning, statistics, and computer science: Improve customer and service provider matching. Identifying better matches between customers and service providers has an incredible impact on the experience of customers and professionals transacting on our platform. The challenge Thumbtack constantly works to balance supply and demand across thousands of local markets and hundreds of service categories. As an Applied Scientist on Pro Growth, you’ll build models and experiments that shape who joins Thumbtack, how they get activated, how we forecast supply needs by market and trade, and how we accelerate time-to-value for new pros. We leverage machine learning, causal inference, and optimization to strategically grow and shape our pro supply base. Our work directly contributes to meeting demand projections, unlocking strategic partnerships, and ultimately enhancing customer experience and platform growth by ensuring a robust and high-quality supply of pros. You’ll work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineers, product managers, and other applied scientists on a portfolio that ranges from incrementality and market forecasting to LLM-powered onboarding agents. You’ll own end-to-end: from problem framing, through experiment design, through deploying models to production, through measuring business impact. jobs.title: Staff Analyst - Risk and Fraud Systems
jobs.description: What do we do? Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. That means we take away 100% of the pain of payment fragmentation. It’s faster, safer, cheaper, and, above all, way better. We’re backed by investors including KKR, FTV Capital, Kindred, Notion, and 83North and serve over 10,000 software sellers in 245 territories globally. The Role: Build the data, decisioning and automated systems that allow Paddle to take more good risk while reducing fraud losses, unnecessary customer friction and manual work. Paddle’s Merchant of Record model makes risk a critical part of the product and its economics. Seller quality, buyer fraud, payment acceptance, refunds, disputes, reserves and card-scheme exposure cannot be optimised independently. This role will connect those signals, identify where the largest value is being lost, turn risk priorities into working controls and workflows, prove their effect in production, and establish a durable owner once a capability becomes repeatable. This is not a strategy-only role and it is not ownership of a large operational team. It is a hands-on build role at the intersection of risk, data, product, engineering and operations. What you'll do: Work hands-on with SQL (Snowflake, dbt), Python, statistics and modern AI-assisted tools to explore data, test hypotheses, prototype controls and evaluate results. Map the end-to-end seller risk system, its data, decisions, controls, owners and failure points. Establish the baseline before building: fraud losses, alert yield, time-to-detect, exposure at detection and analyst effort, with losses reconciled with Finance. Own the health of live controls: every rule and check has an owner, an expected volume, a measured yield and alerting when it goes quiet or drifts, and every change is tested and impact-assessed before release. Build and maintain a labelled library of confirmed fraud cases and a shared fraud typology: the basis for rules now and for machine-learning models with Data Science later. Build a value-ranked portfolio of risk opportunities. Translate risk problems into clear product, data and engineering work with measurable acceptance criteria. Design seller risk tiers that set payout timing, reserves and limits, giving good sellers more room and tightening controls on riskier ones. Backtest rules and risk scores on point-in-time data, and design control experiments, shadow tests and phased roll-outs that measure both loss reduction and legitimate-customer impact. Produce decision artefacts that let senior leaders make trade-offs about risk appetite, engineering investment, customer experience and commercial growth. Stay with each major capability until it works in production, then establish its long-term owner and move to the next high-value problem. Expected 6 month outcomes: At least one major seller-risk journey has materially improved on agreed loss, approval, speed or manual-effort measures. Fraud/Risk Operations spends significantly less time on repetitive screening and more time on investigation, judgement and improvement. Stable capabilities have been handed to durable owners, leaving the role free to take on the next high-value problems. We'd love to hear from you if you: Significant experience building or improving merchant- or seller-side fraud detection at a PSP, acquirer, payfac, marketplace or Merchant of Record, and a working knowledge of how bust-out, transaction laundering and self-dealing show up in the data. Strong hands-on analytical ability, fluency in SQL (Snowflake, dbt or similar), Python and statistics, plus experience using LLMs on unstructured data such as website content or support tickets, with measured accuracy. We started with co-branded credit cards and rebuilt them to be smarter, more rewarding, and brand-first. We partner with companies like Crate & Barrel, Rakuten, Booking.com , H-E-B, Fetch, and Shell to launch modern credit programs that deepen loyalty, unlock savings, and drive growth. But the card is just the beginning. We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank. In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you. As a Fraud Analytics Manager , you will own the analytics function supporting fraud, credit risk, and operations at Imprint. This is a hands-on individual contributor role with managerial scope, focused on building automation, tooling, and reporting infrastructure that reduces manual work and drives faster, smarter decisions across the team. We are a Silicon Valley-based startup headquartered in San Francisco, with operations in Canada, the UK, multiple EU countries and a tech hub in Poland. We are a Deep Learning-first company. Our mission is to automate and optimize brick-and-mortar retail using deep learning computer vision. Focal Systems has been deployed at scale with some of the top retailers in the world, processing hundreds of millions of images per day across tens of thousands of stores globally. We were recently named Confluent's inaugural Data Streaming Startup of the Year, a recognition of how seriously we take the engineering challenges at the core of our business. We seek smart, creative, and passionate people who want to help build a great and enduring company. What We're Looking For We are looking for a Platform Engineer to own the platform that every image from every store passes through: ingestion, Kafka streaming, Python services, GPU model inference, databases, storage, and the GCP and Kubernetes layer underneath. The team is small, so there is no separate SRE, DBA or release team. When a pipeline slows down, you find out whether the cause is a Kafka consumer, a MySQL query, an autoscaler or a node pool, and you fix it, including in the application code. The role is cloud-only, with no on-prem or datacenter hardware, and CI/CD pipelines are a small part of it. The core challenge is scale. We are processing hundreds of millions of images per day across tens of thousands of retail locations globally, and that number is growing fast. Load will grow by an order of magnitude, and your job is to make sure cost and operational effort do not grow with it. What You Will Do Own the design, operation and cost of Focal's production platform on GCP: Kubernetes, Kafka, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, object storage. Drive measurable reductions in COGS and latency, for example lowering GPU inference cost per store through machine types, batching, autoscaling or scheduling, and report the numbers. Read, debug and change Python (FastAPI, Kafka consumers) backend services. Platform problems are often fixed in application code, for example a MySQL query that ran fine at 1,000 stores and times out at 10,000. Fix throughput bottlenecks such as consumer lag at store opening, whether the cause is partition count, consumer throughput, a downstream database or autoscaling reaction time. Rework metrics, alerts and dashboards so the on-call engineer can tell which stores and regions are affected when an alert fires. Take part in incident response, postmortems and capacity planning. Build tooling that gives engineers access to data across regions and storage systems in minutes instead of days. Maintain infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Helm) and the deployment path to production, and work with the backend, deep learning and edge teams so the platform keeps up with new products and models. What You Need to Be Successful Must have Python as a software engineer, not only for scripting. You will contribute to backend code every week. 5+ years building and operating production backend systems on a cloud platform. GCP preferred; deep AWS or Azure experience is fine. Hands-on production experience operating at least one stateful system under load: Kafka or another streaming platform, MySQL/PostgreSQL, or MongoDB. We mean partitioning, replication, lag, slow queries and failover, not only provisioning. Kubernetes in production, including scheduling, resource limits, autoscaling with KEDA, GPU node pools and debugging misbehaving pods. jobs.title: Product Security Engineer
jobs.description: About the role We are seeking a hands-on Security Engineer who thrives in a startup environment. Identify attack surfaces, model adversary behavior, and define what needs to be hardened before launch. Vulnerability Triage & Remediation : Own the end-to-end lifecycle of findings — from discovery through severity assessment, developer-facing write-ups, remediation guidance, and verification of fixes. Coordinate with engineers so issues actually get closed. Vulnerability Disclosure & Bug Bounty : Manage incoming whitehat reports, validate findings by reproducing them, assess severity, communicate with researchers. AI Tools Security Support : Assess technical risks related to AI tools used within teams (such as data exfiltration, prompt injection, training-on-input), maintain security baselines for AI coding tools and review AI-powered internal tools. Qualifications Must-have 5+ years of hands-on experience with a focus on application security, penetration testing, or product security. Demonstrated ability to find vulnerabilities — through manual testing, architecture and/or code review, or creative attack simulation. You should understand order book mechanics, transaction flows, wallet security, and the threat landscape specific to trading infrastructure. Scripting and automation ability — you write tools and automate to scale security across the stack, not just audit and write reports. Experience triaging vulnerabilities and writing clear, actionable remediation guidance for developers. Strong written communication in English — you'll write tickets, assessment reports and researcher responses. Strong plus Experience with cloud infrastructure security — least-privilege enforcement, network security, secrets management. Experience with container security — network policies, RBAC, pod security standards, image scanning, Dockerfile hardening, base image management. Ability to read and review code in at least one of: TypeScript/JavaScript, Solidity, Rust. Understanding of software supply chain security, including dependency ri

jobs.title: Architecture & Performance Modeling Engineer, AI Inference Silicon (Senior / Pri
jobs.description: About Positron AI Positron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference. Chips built for the training era keep running into two walls at inference time: memory bandwidth and chip-to-chip networking. We designed our architecture to break through both. Our first-generation Atlas systems are already in production on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Asimov, our first custom ASIC, takes that architecture to silicon. In simulations, Asimov delivers several times more tokens per dollar and tokens per watt than leading GPUs, at a fraction of the power. Paired in our Titan system, Asimov is built to serve models beyond 16 trillion parameters. In September 2026, we raised $875 million at a $5 billion valuation. NEA led the round, joined by Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners, and others, to bring Asimov and Titan to market. Our team includes engineers from Groq, Lambda, NVIDIA, Meta, F5, and many other industry leaders. Role Overview As a Senior Architecture & Performance Modeling Engineer, you will help shape the architecture of our next-generation AI inference accelerators. You will work directly with chip architects to explore architectural options, quantify tradeoffs, identify bottlenecks, and turn modeling results into actionable design recommendations. This work starts before RTL exists. You will use analytical models and our in-house simulators to answer architectural questions quickly, then refine and validate those models as the design matures. Each engineer on the team takes primary modeling responsibility for a next-generation chip while contributing to a shared modeling framework. Key Responsibilities Architecture Studies and Recommendations Partner with architects to turn design questions into focused modeling studies with clear assumptions, alternatives, metrics, and recommendations. Perform what-if analysis across compute engines, memory capacity and bandwidth, dataflow, DMA, command processing, on-chip interconnect, and chip-to-chip communication. Compare architectural options, explain performance sensitivities, and recommend changes within the system, power, area, and implementation constraints established with the architecture team. Workload Analysis Evaluate representative AI inference workloads across prefill and decode, batch sizes, context lengths, and dense and mixture-of-experts models to identify what limits latency, throughput, and hardware utilization. Provide timely feedback throughout the design cycle by communicating findings, investigating unexpected results, and updating studies as workloads and architectural choices evolve. Model Development and Correlation Develop and extend analytical, transaction-level, and cycle-level models, choosing the level of detail needed to answer each question with useful turnaround time. Maintain reusable models in our native Rust simulator and correlate predictions against RTL simulation, emulation, or silicon measurements as they become available, with regression coverage and clear documentation of assumptions, limitations, and discrepancies. Required Qualifications 5+ years of experience in computer architecture, microarchitecture, or performance modeling for accelerators, CPUs, or GPUs. Demonstrated experience using models to influence architectural decisions, such as identifying a bottleneck, comparing design alternatives, or recommending a change backed by quantitative analysis. A strong understanding of pipelines, queues, parallel execution, memory hierarchies, data movement, and interconnects. Hands-on experience building analytical, transaction-level, or cycle-level performance models, including first-order estimates that help validate and explain simulation results. Comfort working with incomplete specifications, making assumptions explicit, and balancing modeling fidelity with speed of iteration. Strong Rust skills, or expert-level C/C++ skills and a will

Accruals, balance sheet reconciliation and certification, and journal posting with its posting controls. The integration design with SAP S/4HANA or ECC and the other source systems, through APIs, files and middleware. Security and controls designed in: role-based access, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Monitoring, recovery and the non-functional design that keeps the close running. Leading the engineers through build, and reviewing what they deliver against the design at design-authority and go-live checkpoints. Test strategy and acceptance criteria with the finance users. What you bring Solution design on the Redwood platform under any of its names: RunMyJobs, SAP BPA by Redwood, SAP CPS or Cronacle. Design of an automated SAP FI/CO period-end close, where you ran the design workshops and wrote the design yourself. Controls built into your designs: role-based security, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Leading engineers from an approved design through build, testing and go-live. 8 or more years in SAP finance systems, finance automation or record-to-report process design. Useful but not essential: Redwood Finance Automation (RunMyFinance). A BPA-to-RunMyJobs migration. CPS or Redwood tasks run from the SAP Financial Closing cockpit, or SAP Advanced Financial Closing. Financial services or another regulated industry. How to respond Apply with your CV and your available start date. With it, add three lines on your most recent Redwood or SAP close automation project: which Redwood product it ran on, the finance processes in scope, and which design decisions were yours. The work covers the record-to-report cycle: accruals, balance sheet reconciliation, journal posting and the period-end close, all driven into SAP S/4HANA and ECC. You will own the solution design. Accruals, balance sheet reconciliation and certification, and journal posting with its posting controls. The integration design with SAP S/4HANA or ECC and the other source systems, through APIs, files and middleware. Security and controls designed in: role-based access, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Monitoring, recovery and the non-functional design that keeps the close running. Leading the engineers through build, and reviewing what they deliver against the design at design-authority and go-live checkpoints. Test strategy and acceptance criteria with the finance users. What you bring Solution design on the Redwood platform under any of its names: RunMyJobs, SAP BPA by Redwood, SAP CPS or Cronacle. Design of an automated SAP FI/CO period-end close, where you ran the design workshops and wrote the design yourself. Controls built into your designs: role-based security, segregation of duties, audit trails and SOX-aligned evidence. Working alongside a team of deeply technical product marketers who own positioning for AI traffic management, agent identity, and AI observability, you'll plan the launches, campaigns, and content that drive pipeline. This is a high-leverage execution role. What You'll Do: Own launch execution across the AI portfolio — Manage the launch calendar, tiering framework, and cross-functional launch process for all AI product releases, coordinating inputs from technical PMM specialists into cohesive go-to-market moments. You will be the senior design presence within each engagement. You will help turn complex, sometimes ambiguous business and product challenges into clear design direction, guide the team toward high-quality outcomes, and represent the work confidently with senior client stakeholders. This is a hands-on leadership role. You will stay actively involved in the work by shaping direction, reviewing and improving design, facilitating key decisions, solving difficult product problems, and stepping directly into execution where your contribution will have the greatest impact. At the same time, you will own and actively manage key client stakeholders. You will build trust, navigate competing priorities, create alignment, and help stakeholders make good decisions. As a Lead Product Designer at DNA.inc , we expect you to contribute in these key areas: Lead the team Provide clear direction across complex product challenges and help the team move from ambiguity to focused execution. Stay close to the craft, contributing directly where your involvement improves the quality or pace of the work. Set and maintain a high bar for interaction, visual design, prototyping, and product thinking. Give designers clear, useful direction while creating enough space for them to own and develop their work. Mentor and develop other designers through active collaboration, feedback, critique, and hands-on problem solving. Identify gaps in how the team works and establish patterns, systems, or practices that improve quality and consistency beyond a single deliverable. Work closely with Product and Engineering to balance user needs, business goals, technical constraints, and delivery realities. Lead the work Act as a trusted partner to key client stakeholders and independently lead important design conversations. Understand the wider business and organizational context behind the brief, and help stakeholders clarify what really needs to be solved. Turn competing priorities, incomplete information, and differing perspectives into a clear path forward. Present recommendations with conviction, adapt your communication to different audiences, and make the reasoning behind design decisions easy to understand. Navigate pushback, organizational complexity, and stakeholder disagreement while maintaining productive relationships. Build confidence in the team and the work through clear communication, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through. Identify opportunities beyond the immediate request and help connect design decisions to broader product and business outcomes. Strengthen the wider engagement Help strengthen how design operates across the client account, improving the quality and effectiveness of the wider engagement. Work with DNA.inc colleagues across design, product, and engineering to improve the way we deliver together. Share patterns, lessons, and approaches that can strengthen DNA.inc ’s wider design practice.
